Having exposure to carpentry (both her father and
husband had careers as carpenters), Goode used innovative
design to simplify the desk-to-bed conversion. Essentially,
the piece consisted of three tiers. At the bottom was the
base, the width of the base dictated the width of the
unfolded bed. A cabinet on top of the base housed a
mattress folded into thirds, and on top of the cabinet were
the writing surface and storage cubbies that made the piece
To turn the desk into a bed, one had to first lift the
desk’s writing surface, which was connected to the back
of the piece with hinges, and push it up and back until it
stood upright, perpendicular to the floor. For example,
the now-vertical writing surface could serve as the bed’s
Attached to the base with hinges, the front and
back walls of the cabinet could be pushed down
to create a platform the length of a standard-size bed.
